desc:
Build a long array by writing nums one after another k times (so its length is n * k). An inversion is a pair of positions p < q in that long array whose values satisfy value[p] > value[q]. Return the number of inversions in the long array, modulo 1,000,000,007.

k can be huge, so the long array cannot be built.

nums = [2, 1], k = 3   long array [2,1,2,1,2,1]  -> 6
nums = [1, 2], k = 2   long array [1,2,1,2]      -> 1
nums = [4], k = 5      -> 0
hints: Look at an inversion in the long array. Its two positions are either in the same copy of nums or in two different copies. Count each case separately.

Inside one copy, the number of inversions is the ordinary inversion count inv of nums, and there are k copies. For two different copies (an earlier and a later one), what matters is how many pairs (x, y) of elements of nums have x > y, regardless of their order in nums.
Let P be the number of index pairs (a, b) (any order) with nums[a] > nums[b]; it equals C(n,2) minus the pairs of equal values. The answer is k * inv + C(k,2) * P modulo 1,000,000,007.
editorial: Pairs in the same copy: each copy contributes the ordinary inversion count inv, so k copies give k * inv. Pairs in different copies: choose an earlier copy and a later copy in C(k,2) ways; for such a choice, any element x of the earlier copy and any element y of the later copy form an inversion when x > y, regardless of their indices. The number of such ordered choices is P = #{(a, b): nums[a] > nums[b]}.

Every unordered pair of positions with different values contributes exactly one such ordered pair, so P = C(n,2) - sum over values v of C(cnt_v, 2). The inversion count inv comes from merge sort in O(n log n). Finally combine with big integers or modular arithmetic: (k * inv + (k(k-1)/2) * P) mod 1,000,000,007. Beware that C(k,2) is about 5 × 1017 and the product overflows 64 bits unless reduced first.
Time O(n log n), space O(n).
solution:
def repeatedInversions(nums, k):
    from collections import Counter
    M = 1000000007
    n = len(nums)
    a = nums[:]
    buf = a[:]
    inv = 0
    width = 1
    while width < n:
        for lo in range(0, n, 2 * width):
            mid = min(lo + width, n)
            hi = min(lo + 2 * width, n)
            i, j, t = lo, mid, lo
            while i < mid and j < hi:
                if a[i] <= a[j]:
                    buf[t] = a[i]
                    i += 1
                else:
                    buf[t] = a[j]
                    j += 1
                    inv += mid - i
                t += 1
            while i < mid:
                buf[t] = a[i]
                i += 1
                t += 1
            while j < hi:
                buf[t] = a[j]
                j += 1
                t += 1
        a, buf = buf, a
        width *= 2
    pairs = n * (n - 1) // 2 - sum(c * (c - 1) // 2 for c in Counter(nums).values())
    return (k * inv + (k * (k - 1) // 2) % M * pairs) % M
